strategy.summary: GET /products filters the in-memory catalogue by a case-insensitive name substring `q`, pages with `limit`/`offset` (default 20, capped at MAX_LIMIT), returns `{ total, items }`, and refuses non-whole-number limit/offset or limit < 1 with 400. Tests start the real app in-process on an OS-chosen port (as the existing spec does) and assert against expectations derived from the exported PRODUCTS catalogue and MAX_LIMIT/DEFAULT_LIMIT constants.
inScope: GET /products search by q (case-insensitive substring, no q lists all)
Paging with limit/offset, total count, default limit, cap on large limits
400 for non-whole-number limit/offset and limit below 1
outOfScope: GET /products/:id and POST /orders (not part of this ticket)
assumptions: The code's cap (MAX_LIMIT = 50 in src/app.js) is the intended one, not the README's 'up to 100'; asked the reviewer as Q1. Tests import MAX_LIMIT so they follow the code.
No services are faked: the real app runs in-process via createApp() on port 0, and expected results are computed from the exported PRODUCTS catalogue (read-only for GET /products).
Results are in catalogue (id) order, as the README states and the code does (filter preserves order).
openQuestions: README says limit goes up to 100; code caps at 50. Which is intended? (Q1)
Is a negative offset meant to be refused? The code refuses it with 400 (not a whole number); the ticket doesn't say. Tested as the code behaves.

risks.description: Cap mismatch between README (100) and code (50) means clients may request more than they get
risks.mitigation: TC5 pins the cap to the exported MAX_LIMIT and checks the response size equals it

risks.description: Case-sensitive or exact matching would break shop search
risks.mitigation: TC1 uses mixed case query and compares against the catalogue filtered case-insensitively
TC6-TC8 cover decimal, non-numeric, negative and zero values

acceptanceCriteria.text: `q` returns exactly the products whose name contains it, case-insensitively; without `q` every product is matched.
Results are paged by `limit` and `offset`, the response's `total` is the number of matches regardless of paging, and a limit above the cap returns at most the cap.
A `limit` or `offset` that isn't a whole number, or a `limit` below 1, gets 400.

testCases.title: matches names containing q in any case
preconditions: App listening on an OS-chosen port
testCases.expected: 200; total equals the count of PRODUCTS whose lowercased name includes 'teapot' (15); items are exactly those products in id order

testCases.title: lists every product when q is absent
testCases.expected: 200; total equals PRODUCTS.length (120); items are the first DEFAULT_LIMIT products
testCases.rationale: Unfiltered listing and default page size

testCases.title: returns no items and a zero total when nothing matches q
steps: GET /products?q=<a string no product name contains, URL-encoded>
testCases.rationale: Search must not fall back to listing everything

testCases.title: pages through matches with limit and offset and reports the total
testCases.expected: Each response has total 15; pages are the matching products slices [0,4), [4,8), [12,15) (last page short)
testCases.rationale: Paging and total are what the search box needs

testCases.title: caps a large limit at MAX_LIMIT
testCases.expected: 200; items length equals MAX_LIMIT (50) and are the first MAX_LIMIT products; total 120
testCases.rationale: Cap protects the server; README/code disagree on value

testCases.title: returns an empty page with the total when offset is past the last match
refuses a limit that is not a whole number with 400
refuses an offset that is not a whole number with 400
accepts limit 1 and offset 0
testCases.expected: 200 with total 120 and items equal to [PRODUCTS[0]]
testCases.rationale: Refusal boundary must not catch the smallest valid values

strategy.environmentNotes: No external services. Tests start createApp() in-process on port 0 like test/products.test.js; run with `npm test`.
